cap_confirmation: driver reported level_cap 36; Exeggutor-Alola / Dracozolt / Altaria at offset +1 -> L35 and Dragonair at +5 -> L39, all equal 36 + offset - 2 (Medium). No --cap adjustment needed.

attempts.note: 4-0 in five turns without losing a Pokemon. This is an ace-class trainer with a Mega showcase and it did not take a single member off me; my lowest survivor finished at 20/136 and that was from a Flamethrower, not from anything the plan intended.

strategy_checks.check: Mega Altaria actually Mega Evolves and executes (the showcase)
strategy_checks.result: PASS for the transformation, PARTIAL for the plan
strategy_checks.evidence: T2 'The opposing Altaria has Mega Evolved into Mega Altaria!' with the ability correctly becoming PIXILATE and the typing becoming Dragon/Fairy. It then chose Protect on that turn and Double-Edge (Pixilate-converted) on T4. It never reached Dragon Dance, so the 'Dragon Dance / Mega mode' half of the authored plan did not happen. Denying a safe Dragon Dance is the dossier's own named counterplay and it worked, but it worked because Altaria spent its Mega turn guarding rather than setting up.

strategy_checks.check: Alolan Exeggutor's Harvest recycles its own Sitrus
strategy_checks.evidence: T1 'The opposing Exeggutor harvested its Sitrus~Berry!' after consuming it. The recycling loop is live exactly as the dossier describes.

strategy_checks.check: Exeggutor uses Helping Hand only when Dracozolt's attack benefits more than a second attack, otherwise special coverage
strategy_checks.evidence: It never used Helping Hand. On T1 it chose Flamethrower into my Steel-type Excadrill (2x) rather than supporting a Dracozolt that was about to die, and on T2/T3 it chose Giga Drain into Magnezone. Correct restraint - the conditional is being evaluated, not defaulted to.

strategy_checks.check: Dracozolt's Hustle Bolt Beak, and the moved-first doubling condition
strategy_checks.evidence: Dracozolt's selected move on T1 was MOVE_BOLT_BEAK aimed at my Togekiss, but it was KOed first by a spread Earthquake (Ground is 2x into Electric/Dragon). The dossier's 'interaction to remember' - a Hustle-boosted Bolt Beak from full Speed - never happened. Wide Lens and Hustle were both live on the stat block.

strategy_checks.check: Dragonair's Thunder Wave creates a move-first opportunity on turn two
strategy_checks.evidence: Dragonair entered on T3 and had decision turns on T3 and T4. It chose Protect on T4 and never selected Thunder Wave. This is the member the dossier singles out - 'a pre-evolution whose whole job is to survive long enough to Thunder Wave' - and it is carried at +5, the most expensive offset on the team. It survived perfectly well and then did not do the job. See AI defect 1.

strategy_checks.check: Ground immunity blanks Bolt Beak (dossier crack)
strategy_checks.evidence: Excadrill was led specifically so that Bolt Beak would be a dead move. Dracozolt selected Bolt Beak at Togekiss rather than at the Ground type, which is correct targeting, but died before it resolved.

Togekiss's Dazzling Gleam is 2x into all four members while Altaria is still Dragon/Flying and it took Exeggutor and softened the rest. The moment Altaria Megas into Dragon/Fairy the Steel lane takes over, and one Magnezone Flash Cannon KOed a full-HP 130 HP Mega Altaria outright on T4. That is the whole fight in one line.

protect_ledger.payoff: real - blocked Dazzling Gleam on the turn it Mega Evolved. Defensible in isolation, but it spent the Mega's free turn on a guard rather than the Dragon Dance the plan is built on
real - at 40/133 it blocked Dazzling Gleam, which was lethal

protect_note: Two Protects, both with payoff, no consecutive-use failures and no empty guarding. Cadence is fine; the problem with this team is not its Protects.

ai_defects.board: Dragonair (L39, Eviolite, Shed Skin, 40/133) beside a Mega Altaria that wants to Dragon Dance, against a Magnezone (base 60 Speed) and a Togekiss (base 80) that were both outspeeding its partner
ai_defects.chosen: T4 MOVE_PROTECT; Thunder Wave never selected on either turn
ai_defects.better: MOVE_THUNDER_WAVE into Magnezone or Togekiss. The dossier states plainly that Dragonair's job is to create a move-first opportunity for the team and that this is why it carries a +5 offset and an Eviolite. Paralysis on either of my battlers is the only route this team had to a safe Dragon Dance, which is the other thing it failed to reach.
ai_defects.note: This is the third instance in my block of a non-damaging signature move never being selected - Grapploct's Octolock at E0118 and Froslass's Destiny Bond at E0126 are the others, and Lucas's Ninetales also skipped Aurora Veil for an attack. All four are status or utility moves on trainers whose plan is built around them. Worth checking as one shared scoring question rather than four team-specific ones: the pattern suggests non-damaging moves are being under-valued relative to any available attack.

level_changes.reason: Brief rule 5: first optimized attempt won in four turns with ZERO player faints against an ace-class trainer with a Mega showcase. That is the clearest level-increase trigger in my whole block. Exeggutor is one of the three joint-lowest members at +1; the Mega holder is excluded from a first bump by the brief, so the two non-Mega members at +1 take it. Exeggutor also survived longest of the three and its Harvest loop is worth giving more turns to.

Same trigger. Dracozolt is the second joint-lowest member and it is the one the dossier calls the centrepiece interaction - a Hustle-boosted Bolt Beak from full Speed - which it never got to show because it died on turn one to a spread Earthquake. A level does not fix its 2x Ground weakness but it is the honest smallest lever, and this member more than any other deserves to survive to act. Deliberately NOT applied to Altaria (the Mega, excluded first per the brief) or Dragonair (already +5 and it survived fine - its problem is that it did not use Thunder Wave, which is AI defect 1, and AGENTS.md says fix the defect before compensating with levels).

retest_status: PENDING REBUILD. Both offset changes are in data/emerald_champions/emerald_champions_battle_teams.txt but the headless ROM in work/agent-battle-build-2 predates them. Per this wave's instructions I do not run make; the main agent should re-materialize, rebuild and re-run seed 107 against this manifest. This one matters more than the others in my block: a 4-0 against an ace deserves a confirmed retest, and I would not be surprised if +1 on two members is not enough.
cooler: The concept is genuinely good and the dossier's own 'could this be cooler' answer is right about why - Wide Lens is a clever and correct answer to Hustle, Harvest recycling its own Sitrus while Alolan Exeggutor throws Draco Meteor is a real engine, and Mega Altaria is the right ace for a dragon tamer. I am not proposing to change a species. But I have to be blunt about the result: an ace-class Mega showcase went 4-0 in five turns, and levels are not really the reason. The reason is that all four members are Dragon, which means they share one answer, and the Mega makes it worse rather than better - the instant Altaria Mega Evolves it becomes Dragon/Fairy, and Fairy is 2x to Steel, so a single Flash Cannon from a Magnezone that any player at this stage can have OHKOed it from full HP. The team's own transformation opens its worst hole. Two concrete thoughts for a later pass. First, this roster needs one member that punishes the Steel answer - a Fire or Ground type that a player's Excadrill/Magnezone/Kartana cannot safely sit in front of - so that bringing the obvious Steel lane costs something. Second, and more interesting: Mega Altaria's Dragon Dance never happened in this battle, and it never will while the Mega's free turn is spent guarding. If the intended showcase is a Mega Altaria that dances and then sweeps, it needs a turn bought for it, and Dragonair's Thunder Wave is exactly the move that is supposed to buy it (see AI defect 1). Fix that and this fight changes character completely without touching a single species or level.
